worlds.name: Java Awakening
worlds.summary: Java fluency: methods, classes, collections, streams and tests.

worlds.name: Data Structure Forge
worlds.summary: Arrays, hash tables, lists, stacks, queues, heaps, trees and graphs.

worlds.name: Pattern Kingdom
worlds.summary: Algorithmic patterns and recognising when to use them.

worlds.name: Debug Dungeon
worlds.summary: Broken-code challenges: diagnose, fix minimally, prove it with a test.

skills.name: Methods
skills.definition: Declare methods with parameters and return values, and decompose a requirement into small methods with clear contracts.

skills.name: Conditions
skills.definition: Use if/else and boolean expressions to choose behaviour, including boundary values such as 'at least' versus 'more than'.

skills.name: Loops
skills.definition: Traverse arrays and collections with for, while and enhanced-for loops with correct start and end boundaries.

skills.name: Input validation and exceptions
skills.definition: Reject invalid arguments at a method's boundary by throwing the right unchecked exception with a useful message.

skills.name: Integer arithmetic and overflow
skills.definition: Represent money in integer minor units and detect overflow with exact arithmetic instead of silently wrapping.

skills.name: Classes and objects
skills.definition: Define classes with constructors, fields and instance methods, and create and use objects.

skills.name: Encapsulation
skills.definition: Keep state private and expose behaviour that protects the object's invariants, rather than raw getters and setters.

skills.name: Interfaces and abstraction
skills.definition: Define interfaces that describe a contract and write callers that depend on the interface, not a concrete class.

skills.name: Polymorphism
skills.definition: Call methods through a common type so different runtime implementations supply different behaviour.

skills.name: Inheritance
skills.definition: Extend a suitable base type, override behaviour, and respect substitutability; know when composition is the better choice.

skills.name: Collections
skills.definition: Choose and use List, Set and Map implementations and know the cost of their common operations.

skills.name: Streams
skills.definition: Write map/filter/reduce/collect pipelines, convert loops to streams and back, and explain when a loop is clearer.

skills.name: Unit testing
skills.definition: Write focused JUnit tests that cover boundaries and failure cases, not only the happy path.

skills.name: Strings
skills.definition: Work with immutable Strings, char values, equality (equals vs ==), substring/indexOf/split and StringBuilder for repeated building.

skills.name: Loop analysis
skills.definition: Derive time bounds for loops: linear passes, nested and triangular loops, doubling or halving counters, and independent input sizes.

skills.name: Sliding window
skills.definition: Recognise problems about a contiguous range with a maintainable constraint and solve them in one pass by growing and shrinking a window.

skills.name: Primitives and operators
skills.definition: Use int, long, double, char and boolean correctly: integer division and remainder, casting, overflow, floating-point comparison and boxed-value equality.

skills.name: Recursion analysis
skills.definition: Bound recursive algorithms by their call tree: linear chains, halving, divide and conquer, branching recursion and output-sensitive enumeration.

skills.name: Space and amortized cost
skills.definition: Count auxiliary space including the call stack and copies, separate it from output space, and reason about amortized costs such as dynamic-array growth.

skills.name: Choosing data structures
skills.definition: Pick a structure from what the operations need: key lookup, ordering, first-in-first-out, last-in-first-out, priority or membership, and say why.

skills.name: Hashing
skills.definition: Use hash maps and sets for frequencies, complements, grouping and de-duplication to trade memory for linear time.

skills.name: Binary search
skills.definition: Halve a search space that has a monotone condition: sorted arrays, first/last occurrence and searching on the answer.

skills.name: Graph search
skills.definition: Choose and apply BFS or DFS on graphs and grids: shortest paths with equal costs, reachability, components and cycle detection.

skills.name: Hash tables
skills.definition: How hashing, buckets, collisions, load factor and resizing give O(1) average operations, and the equals/hashCode contract that makes them work.

skills.name: Stacks, queues and deques
skills.definition: Last-in-first-out and first-in-first-out structures, Java's ArrayDeque, and problems they fit: matching brackets, undo, monotonic stacks, level-by-level processing.

skills.name: Heaps and priority queues
skills.definition: Min- and max-heaps, PriorityQueue, O(log n) insert and remove-min, Top K and k-way merging.

skills.name: Trees and traversals
skills.definition: Binary trees and binary search trees: terminology, recursive and level-order traversals, height, and why balance matters.

skills.name: Graph representations
skills.definition: Represent graphs as adjacency lists, matrices or edge lists and choose by size and density.

skills.name: Two pointers
skills.definition: Move two indices through an array or string (towards each other or in the same direction) to solve pair, partition and palindrome problems in one pass.

skills.name: Debugging
skills.definition: Go from a symptom to a root cause, make the smallest fix that removes it, and pin it down with a test that failed before the fix.

skills.name: Networking
skills.definition: Clients and servers, DNS, TCP and UDP, HTTP methods and status codes, REST, WebSockets and server-sent events, proxies and CDNs.

skills.name: Scaling and storage
skills.definition: Vertical and horizontal scaling, stateless services and load balancing; SQL and NoSQL, indexes, replication and partitioning, with their trade-offs.

skills.name: Caching and queues
skills.definition: Cache-aside, TTLs and invalidation, write strategies, stampedes; message queues for decoupling, at-least-once delivery and idempotent consumers.

skills.name: Capacity estimation
skills.definition: Turn users and behaviour into QPS, storage, bandwidth and cache size with stated assumptions and units.

skills.name: Design recognition
skills.definition: Map requirements to candidate components (CDN, cache, queue, partitioning, replicas) and justify them with trade-offs rather than cues alone.

skills.name: Design reasoning
skills.definition: Turn requirements into a design and defend it under follow-up: growth, read and write paths, fan-out, failure, duplicates and cost, with explicit trade-offs.

skills.name: Building caches
skills.definition: Implement bounded and expiring caches with explicit eviction rules, O(1) operations and testable time.

skills.name: Rate limiting
skills.definition: Implement token-bucket and window limiters with integer time arithmetic and clear refill rules.

skills.name: Job scheduling
skills.definition: Order and dispatch work fairly: priorities, stable tie-breaking and bounded queues.

skills.name: Object modeling
skills.definition: Turn requirements into classes with clear ownership of state and rules, validating before changing state.

skills.name: Designing for change
skills.definition: Absorb a new requirement with a small, local change: data-driven rules, extension points and preserved behaviour.

skills.name: Design patterns in practice
skills.definition: Choose Strategy, Observer, Adapter, Decorator, State and others when a requirement calls for them, and know their costs.

skills.name: Behavioral answers
skills.definition: Tell true stories in STAR form with your own role clear, honest results and what you learned, in 1 to 3 minutes.
